references.text: Earlier law in the Torah about helping an enemy's ox or donkey that has gone astray or fallen under its burden, which is expanded in Deuteronomy to apply to a brother's animal
The fundamental command to love your neighbor as yourself, which serves as the ethical foundation for returning lost animals to their owner
Prophetic criticism of shepherds who do not seek after the scattered, in contrast to the command to bring back what has gone astray
God's promise to seek out the scattered and bring them back, reflecting the principle in this commandment
Jesus' parable of the lost sheep illustrating God's care for those who have wandered away, based on the principle of seeking what is lost
The parable of the lost sheep in Luke, showing the same concern to find and bring back what has gone astray
